messages.content: The Friday overnight flight is too awkward once luggage is included. Put me back on the Saturday morning nonstop and compare the three-night hotel choices.

Understood. I’ll use the Wednesday morning nonstop to Atlanta, three hotel nights, and the Saturday 12:40 p.m. nonstop home. The three lodging options are the Emory Inn by the Thursday workshop, a lower-priced hotel near Decatur rail, and the Courtyard near the Friday author event. Is Mateo still joining you?
Yes, he is. We’ll share one room, but for this Atlanta trip only please get two separate beds. His sleep schedule will be different while I’m at the workshop.
I’ll compare one room with two beds for this trip. Current tax-inclusive totals are $603 at the Emory Inn, $548 at the Decatur rail hotel, and $642 at the Courtyard near the author venue.
How do those work for Thursday and Friday transportation? The workshops start early Thursday, and the author event ends at 7:30 Friday.

The Emory Inn is about a 7-minute walk from Thursday’s sessions; Friday would require a roughly 15-minute car each way. The rail hotel is about 25 minutes from the workshop by bus and walking, but only one rail stop plus a short walk from Friday’s venue. The Courtyard is a 3-minute walk from the author event, while Thursday would require a 12- to 18-minute car each way.
Please add the likely transportation rather than comparing room prices alone.

Using conservative estimates for both of you: Emory Inn is about $653 including Friday cars; the rail hotel is about $588 including Thursday local transit and a short Wednesday car from the airport rail connection; the Courtyard is about $712 including Thursday cars. Saturday airport travel is similar from all three and is not included because each can use rail or a car.
What happens with our bags Wednesday? We arrive at 1:04, well before the 5:00 registration.

All three confirmed that registered guests may leave luggage at the front desk before the room is ready, at no charge. Check-in begins at 3:00 p.m. at the Emory Inn and Courtyard and 4:00 p.m. at the rail hotel. The Emory Inn gives you the simplest path: leave the bags, have lunch nearby, and walk to registration.
And Saturday? I don’t want breakfast or checkout to make the 12:40 flight tight.

Each has an 11:00 a.m. checkout, so you can leave around 9:35 to 9:45 a.m. without requesting late checkout. The Emory Inn serves breakfast from 6:30 a.m.; it is not included and is currently $18 per person. The rail hotel starts complimentary breakfast at 7:00. The Courtyard café opens at 6:30, with items charged separately.
The savings at the rail hotel are not enough for that Thursday commute. Choose the Emory Inn, confirm the two-bed room and cancellation terms, and book it if there is no mandatory fee due on site.

The Emory Inn has a room with two queen beds for Wednesday, November 18 through Saturday, November 21. The total is $603 including taxes, with no mandatory property or destination fee due on site. Cancellation is permitted without charge until 6:00 p.m. local time on Monday, November 16; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. I booked it for Elena Ruiz and Mateo Ruiz. The hotel confirmation records three nights, two queen beds, early luggage storage on Wednesday, and 11:00 a.m. Saturday checkout. Your working itinerary is now the Wednesday 8:05 a.m. nonstop to Atlanta, 5:00 p.m. registration, Thursday workshops, the Friday author event ending at 7:30 p.m., and the Saturday 12:40 p.m. nonstop to Denver. The flights still need final schedule, operating-carrier, baggage, and seat verification.
